input.quote: 15. ASSIGNMENT OR TRANSFER. Neither party shall assign or transfer any of its rights under this Agreement without the prior written approval of the other party, except no such approval shall be required for an assignment to a financially responsible affiliate.
input.rationale: Section 15 is the only assignment provision and there is no change-of-control clause anywhere in the Agreement (so no Vendor exit or re-pricing right — that element is acceptable). However, the clause fails the fallback on two material terms: it gives Client no carve-out for a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets (only a "financially responsible affiliate"), and the consent requirement binding Client is unqualified rather than "not to be unreasonably withheld." A consent-gated prohibition with no M&A carve-out sits at the edge of walk-away territory. Our redline adds the affiliate/successor carve-out for Client, the reasonableness standard on consent, a bar on TrueLink assigning to a Client competitor, and express confirmation that a Client change of control is not an assignment and triggers no TrueLink termination or re-pricing right. If TrueLink prefers symmetry, we can fall back to a mutual successor right exercisable on written notice with reasonable consent for other assignments.

ops.oldText: Neither party shall assign or transfer any of its rights under this Agreement without the prior written approval of the other party, except no such approval shall be required for an assignment to a financially responsible affiliate.
ops.newText: Neither party shall assign or transfer any of its rights under this Agreement without the prior written approval of the other party, which approval shall not be unreasonably withheld or delayed, except no such approval shall be required for an assignment by Client to a financially responsible affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all of its assets. TrueLink shall not assign or transfer this Agreement to a competitor of Client. No change of control of Client shall constitute an assignment requiring approval or give rise to any right of TrueLink to terminate, suspend or re-price this Agreement.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We added the customary affiliate and merger/successor carve-out for Client, a reasonableness standard on consent, and confirmation that a change of control of Client is not an assignment and gives TrueLink no termination or re-pricing right; we can accept a mutual notice-based successor right as a fallback.
proposal.summary: Add Client affiliate/successor assignment carve-out, reasonable-consent standard, no assignment by Vendor to a Client competitor, and change-of-control protection.
